records.finding: Manufacturer documentation explicitly lists a 12-degree horizontal reflection stage VR1-HRS and a separate 12-degree absolute-reflectance stage VR1-VWA-12. Therefore the paper's angle is not evidence that a current 12.5-degree product should be substituted.
records.unresolved: The paper does not identify which exact legacy stage/base/spectrometer adapter was installed. The two candidates have different optical paths and sample handling. Overall and mounting dimensions remain missing.
records.candidate_decision: VR1-HRS plus a separately reconstructed FTIR optical base is an authored demo choice. It is not identified as the paper's exact variant; mounting and dimensions remain open.
records.additional_finding: The current manufacturer page identifies VR1-HRS and supplied 3, 6 and 13 mm aperture masks. These dimensions do not establish the outer stage, legacy optical base or spectrometer mating dimensions.

records.finding: 36 AWG is listed as 0.13 mm conductor diameter; the ordering note maps the length suffix 36 to 1 m (40 inches). Do not infer exact lead length simply by reading the suffix as inches.
records.unresolved: Flexible cable mechanics, extension conductor pairs, actual terminations, strain relief and sensor stream remain open.

records.unresolved: Geometry availability does not resolve compound resource completeness, contact parameters, wiring, compliant lining or full campaign quantity allocation.

records.finding: The Thermo-hosted VeeMax manual explicitly identifies PIKE Technologies. Its availability is not evidence that VeeMax is the paper's Spectra-Tech accessory. Do not silently replace the reported manufacturer.
records.unresolved: Exact historical paper SKU, outer/mounting dimensions, Nicolet adapter, coupled mirrors, optical calibration and sample retention.
records.candidate_decision: The inspected manufacturer catalogue shows four independent mirrors (M1/M2/M3/M5) and M4 as the specimen/reference surface. The former extra M4 mirror plus separate specimen is preserved as a rejected topology. The Nicolet 6700 manual p54 confirms right-to-left sample-bay optics, supporting 500/0014-010 as a demo candidate. The selected common M3/M4 rotor still misses the finite faces at four of five inspected angles; exact linkage, adapter and historical paper identity remain unresolved.
